source_snapshot.procedure: Uses fixed socket/die/NBIO/core/port 0:0:1/3/0 and proprietary errortype0/1 for LCRC TX/RX.
source_snapshot.criteria: Tool PASS plus an OS correctable report.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; mixes LCRC, ECRC, poison and fatal log terms.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Adds NIC mapping but lacks authoritative direction flags, directed traffic and counter oracle.

old_problem: The fixed fabric tuple cannot cover slot 1~N, proprietary errortype0/1 direction and observing-side semantics are unproven, and generic OS logging cannot establish TX versus RX replay behavior.
disposition_reason: PCIe defines LCRC checking and replay, but not this AMD tool's errortype0/1 encoding or socket/die/NBIO/core/port selector. Those are core command semantics, not mere runtime values, and ED-03 forbids guessing them. Without an attributable directional counter or approved analyzer oracle, PASS cannot distinguish TX from RX. Pending/BLOCKED remains until the vendor package establishes both the flag mapping and evidence point.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row61, exact AI/history record2462, preceding ECRC cases and next OCP LCRC row62.
Preserved both TX and RX stimuli for every required PCIe slot.
Separated standard LCRC/replay behavior from proprietary direction and fabric-selector semantics.
Required isolated directional traffic, counter baselines and no persistent link degradation.
No NIC installation, BIOS/HDT change, traffic injection, retrain, reset or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: PCIe directional LCRC TX/RX replay and link recovery
test_case.purpose: For each approved PCIe NIC/slot, prove separate TX and RX LCRC stimuli affect the intended link direction, produce the documented replay/counter response and preserve bounded traffic plus stable link health.
required_package: Vendor definition of errortype0/1 and observing-side semantics
Isolated bidirectional traffic and packet-integrity oracle
Direction-specific link/NIC/AER counters or approved analyzer method
Abort thresholds, OOB recovery and exact restoration runbook
test_case.test_command: Do not run the proprietary commands. After vendor approval, baseline mapped link and directional traffic/counters; execute one authorized TX stimulus and, after cleanup, one RX stimulus on one verified port; correlate the receiving-side replay/counter and packet outcome; restore all AER/HDT/BIOS and link state before another slot.
test_case.expected_result: Each approved flag produces the documented direction-specific counter/status delta and bounded replay outcome on the intended link, with no fatal/DPC/SyncFlood escalation, driver reset, persistent packet loss, retrain, width/speed downgrade or residual error.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS until flag/selector semantics and an attributable directional oracle are authoritative. Tool PASS, broad dmesg grep, an unmapped tuple, indistinguishable TX/RX evidence, wrong port, excessive loss or degraded link fails.
safety_gate: Dedicated isolated NIC traffic with independent OOB management.
No use of the literal tuple without live signed mapping.
One direction and port at a time; abort on wrong counter/port, loss, retrain, downgrade, reset or fatal escalation.
No automatic retry; preserve counters and traffic evidence.
expected_evidence: Vendor flag/selector contract and topology map
Separate TX and RX transcripts with observing-side evidence
test_case.recovery: Stop traffic/injection, preserve counters, restore saved AER/severity/SyncFlood/HDT/BIOS state, recover the NIC/link through the approved procedure and verify speed, width, driver and traffic. Execution stays blocked until this path and thresholds are signed.

source_conflict.reason: Vendor TX/RX flags, fabric tuple meaning and direction-specific evidence remain unsupported.

blocked.reason: An unverified selector/flag can hit the wrong link and no authoritative direction oracle exists.
